blocks.text:
Design the core matching engine behind a ride-sharing service (the kind that powers Uber Pool or Lyft Shared style carpooling). The distinguishing challenge is detour-constrained ride pooling: when a rider requests a shared ride, the system should try to fit them into a driver who already has a passenger, but only if doing so adds an acceptable detour to that driver's existing trip, rather than simply matching to whichever driver happens to be nearest.

  • Actors: Rider (requests a solo or pooled ride), RideDispatchService (the core orchestrator).
  • Scope: driver capacity, detour-constrained pooling for shared rides, solo matching, and fare calculation with a pooled discount.

The distinguishing mechanic is a real route-insertion heuristic: a new rider joins an in-progress driver only if the extra distance their pickup and dropoff would add, compared to that driver's original route, stays within a fixed detour tolerance.
The system must support the following core capabilities:

items: Request a solo ride: match to the nearest driver who currently has no other riders.
Request a pooled ride: try to insert the rider into an already-occupied driver's route within an acceptable detour, falling back to the nearest empty driver if no pooling opportunity qualifies.
Complete a ride: free up the driver's occupied seat for future matching.
Calculate fare: price a ride from a base fare plus a per-distance rate, discounted if the ride ended up shared with another rider.
Reject unreasonable manual pooling: a direct pooling request that would exceed the detour limit must be rejected.

blocks.text: Beyond correctness, the design should hold up along five quality pillars:

metadata.alt: Five non-functional pillars: scalability, extensibility, maintainability, performance, thread safety

items: Scalability: supporting thousands of concurrent riders and drivers must not require touching existing matching logic.
Extensibility: a new matching algorithm (multi-stop pooling, surge-aware matching) should plug in without rewriting the service.
Maintainability: matching rules, notification, and id creation are isolated in their own classes.
Performance: evaluating candidate drivers for a new ride request is proportional to the number of tracked drivers.
Thread safety: two riders attempting to pool onto the same driver concurrently must never both slip past that driver's capacity check.

blocks.text: Questions worth asking the interviewer before designing:

items: Should the detour limit be a fixed distance, a percentage of the original trip length, or a maximum added time?
Can more than two riders share a single pooled ride, or is pooling capped at two?
Should a rider be able to opt out of pooling mid-trip if the detour becomes uncomfortable?
Is real road-network distance required, or is straight-line distance an acceptable simplification?
Should surge pricing be layered on top of the base fare and per-distance rate?

blocks.text: To keep the design focused, we make these explicit assumptions:

items: Distance is computed as straight-line Euclidean distance on a flat coordinate plane, a simplification versus real road-network routing.
Pooling is capped at two riders per driver in this design, a reasonable starting point that keeps the route-insertion math tractable.

A driver's active route, once they have picked up their first pooled rider, is represented by that first rider's pickup and dropoff points, the reference segment any further pooling insertion is measured against.

Fare is calculated at ride completion rather than at match time, so a rider who was picked up before a pool partner joined still receives the pooled discount, since the discount reflects the trip's actual final shared status.
A rider cannot opt out of pooling mid-trip in this design, that is noted as a follow-up.

blocks.text: The design centers on four core entities:

metadata.alt: Core entities: Driver, Ride, Rider, and Fare

items: Driver: a courier with a location, a capacity, and the active route of whichever rider they picked up first.
Ride: one rider's trip request, tracking pickup, dropoff, type, and lifecycle status.
Rider: the person requesting a ride, identified within this design simply by name.
Fare: the computed price for one ride, including any pooled discount.

blocks.text: These entities connect through a small set of well-defined relationships:

metadata.alt: A driver carries up to their capacity worth of rides concurrently; each ride is requested by one rider and priced by a fare calculation

items: Driver to Ride is one-to-many, bounded by the driver's capacity at any given moment.
Ride to Rider is many-to-one, a rider can place many ride requests over time.
Ride to Fare is a derived, on-demand relationship computed when calculateFare is called.

blocks.text: Three patterns keep matching rules, notification, and id creation decoupled from the core service.
Why needed: a solo ride and a pooled ride fundamentally disagree on which drivers even qualify, empty-only versus detour-constrained sharing, and that decision genuinely varies per ride request.

metadata.alt: MatchingStrategy interface with DirectMatchingStrategy and PooledMatchingStrategy implementations

blocks.text: Why it is the best fit: a future multi-stop or surge-aware matching algorithm is a new strategy implementation, with zero changes to the core assignment logic in RideDispatchService. What it solves: it isolates ride-type-specific matching rules from the shared, stable assignment and lifecycle-tracking algorithm.
Why needed: a ride being matched, a match failing, or a ride completing are all events a real ride-sharing app would want to react to (rider notifications, driver apps, analytics).

metadata.alt: RideObserver interface notified by RideDispatchService on every lifecycle event

blocks.text: Why it is the best fit: RideDispatchService does not need to know who is listening. What it solves: it decouples the core matching workflow from side effects.
Why needed: ride id generation should not be scattered across calling code.

metadata.alt: RideIdFactory generating sequential RIDE prefixed ids

blocks.text: Why it is the best fit: every ride is created through one consistent path. What it solves: centralizes id-generation rules so they cannot drift or collide.
Each class has a single, clear responsibility:

items: Driver: attributes driverId, locationX, locationY, capacity, currentRiders, activePickupX/Y, activeDropoffX/Y; responsibility: track one courier's occupancy and current route reference segment.
Ride: attributes rideId, riderName, pickupX/Y, dropoffX/Y, type, assignedDriverId, status; responsibility: represent one rider's trip through its lifecycle.
RideDispatchService: the orchestrator; responsibility: match rides, enforce detour and capacity limits, calculate fares, and track lifecycle transitions.

blocks.text: Two interfaces keep the design open for extension:

metadata.alt: MatchingStrategy and RideObserver interfaces with their key methods

items: MatchingStrategy: findDriver(ride, drivers): abstracts away exactly how a driver is selected for a ride request.
RideObserver: onRideMatched / onMatchFailed / onRideCompleted: abstracts away who reacts to lifecycle events.

blocks.text: Three flows below cover a fresh assignment to an empty driver, a successful pooled match within the detour limit, and a manual pooling attempt rejected for exceeding the detour limit.

metadata.alt: Alice's pooled request finds no existing occupied driver to join, so the nearest empty driver, D1, is assigned fresh
Bob's pooled request fits into D1's existing route within the detour limit, so he joins Alice on the same driver
Eve's manual pooling attempt onto a distant driver is rejected for exceeding the detour limit

blocks.text: The pooled-matching workflow, alongside its fallback and failure branches, looks like this:

metadata.alt: A pooled request first tries a detour-constrained insertion into an occupied driver, then falls back to the nearest empty driver, failing only if neither exists

items: Happy path, fresh: request a pooled ride → no occupied driver qualifies → the nearest empty driver is assigned, becoming this driver's reference route.
Happy path, pooled: request a pooled ride → an occupied driver's insertion detour stays within the limit → the rider joins that driver alongside the existing rider.
Failure path: request a ride → no occupied driver qualifies for pooling and no empty driver exists → the match fails.

blocks.text: The service exposes a small, intention-revealing API:

items: requestRide(riderName, pickupX, pickupY, dropoffX, dropoffY, type): matches a new ride request using the strategy appropriate to its type.
poolManually(rideId, driverId): directly attempts to pool a ride onto a specific driver, still detour-checked.
calculateFare(rideId): computes the price for a ride, applying the pooled discount if applicable at call time.
completeRide(rideId): transitions a matched ride to completed, freeing its driver's occupied seat.

blocks.text: Three custom exceptions cover the realistic failure modes:

items: NoDriverAvailableException: neither a qualifying pooled driver nor an empty driver exists.
InvalidRideStateException: completeRide is called on a ride that was never matched.
DetourLimitExceededException: a manual pooling request would add more detour than the configured limit allows.

blocks.text: The critical race is two riders attempting to pool onto the same driver at nearly the same moment.

metadata.alt: Two threads racing to pool onto the same driver; synchronization ensures one join is counted and applied before the other reads the current occupancy

blocks.text: Synchronizing the check-then-increment step per driver ensures two concurrent pooling attempts can never both read an occupancy just below capacity and both proceed, which would otherwise let a driver exceed their seat capacity.
The pattern choices make several future features low-friction to add:

items: A new matching algorithm (multi-stop pooling beyond two riders, surge-aware matching) is a new MatchingStrategy implementation.
A new notification channel (rider push notification, driver app alert) is a new RideObserver implementation.
Mid-trip pooling opt-out can be added as a new lifecycle transition without touching the matching algorithm itself.
Real road-network distance can replace the straight-line calculation by swapping the distance helper, without touching the matching or fare logic that consumes it.
Single Responsibility: Driver tracks occupancy and route reference, MatchingStrategy decides driver selection, RideObserver reacts to events, each for one reason to change.
Open/Closed: new matching algorithms or notification behavior extends via new classes, not edits to RideDispatchService.
Liskov Substitution: any MatchingStrategy or RideObserver implementation can replace another without breaking the service.
Interface Segregation: RideObserver exposes only the three lifecycle callbacks a listener actually needs.
Dependency Inversion: RideDispatchService depends on the MatchingStrategy and RideObserver interfaces, not concrete classes.
A driver exactly at their capacity limit is correctly excluded from further pooling, not just drivers already over it.
A solo ride request never considers an occupied driver at all, even one whose detour would technically qualify, since SOLO explicitly opts out of sharing by design.

Completing a ride correctly frees exactly one seat, allowing a driver who dropped one rider off to immediately be eligible again as either an empty driver or still-occupied pooling candidate depending on remaining riders.
A pooled request when zero drivers are registered at all fails the same way as when every driver is full or detour-ineligible, both reported as NoDriverAvailableException.
requestRide: O(d) where d is the number of registered drivers, scanned to evaluate pooling eligibility and, if needed, the nearest empty driver.
completeRide / calculateFare: O(1).
Space: O(drivers + rides) held in memory.

blocks.text: A relational schema mirrors the in-memory model directly, with foreign keys enforcing referential integrity:

items: An index on Driver(currentRiders, capacity) speeds up scanning for drivers with spare seats.
Ride stores driverId as a foreign key, capturing the full assignment relationship for one trip.
Move from straight-line distance to real road-network travel time for both matching and detour calculation.
Support pooling beyond two riders with a full multi-stop route representation.
Add mid-trip pooling opt-out with an automatic fare recalculation.
In a distributed deployment, shard driver tracking by geographic region rather than scanning every driver for every ride request.

// Whether a ride is willing to share a driver with another rider.
enum RideType { SOLO, POOLED }

// Lifecycle status of a single ride.
enum RideStatus { REQUESTED, MATCHED, COMPLETED }

// A courier with a location, a capacity, and the active route of whoever they picked up first.
class Driver {
    private final String driverId;   // unique id
    private final double locationX;    // base x coordinate
    private final double locationY;      // base y coordinate
    private final int capacity;            // max concurrent riders this driver can carry
    private int currentRiders;               // riders currently on board
    private double activePickupX;              // reference route: first rider's pickup x
    private double activePickupY;                 // reference route: first rider's pickup y
    private double activeDropoffX;                   // reference route: first rider's dropoff x
    private double activeDropoffY;                       // reference route: first rider's dropoff y

    public Driver(String driverId, double locationX, double locationY, int capacity) {
        this.driverId = driverId; // store id
        this.locationX = locationX; // store base x
        this.locationY = locationY;   // store base y
        this.capacity = capacity;       // store capacity
        this.currentRiders = 0;           // starts empty
    }

    public String getDriverId() { return driverId; }             // id getter
    public double getLocationX() { return locationX; }              // base x getter
    public double getLocationY() { return locationY; }                 // base y getter
    public int getCapacity() { return capacity; }                        // capacity getter
    public int getCurrentRiders() { return currentRiders; }                 // rider count getter
    public boolean isEmpty() { return currentRiders == 0; }                    // true if carrying nobody
    public boolean hasSpareSeat() { return currentRiders < capacity; }            // true if room for one more
    public double getActivePickupX() { return activePickupX; }                       // reference pickup x getter
    public double getActivePickupY() { return activePickupY; }                          // reference pickup y getter
    public double getActiveDropoffX() { return activeDropoffX; }                           // reference dropoff x getter
    public double getActiveDropoffY() { return activeDropoffY; }                              // reference dropoff y getter

    public void assignFresh(double pickupX, double pickupY, double dropoffX, double dropoffY) {
        this.activePickupX = pickupX;     // this becomes the reference route's pickup
        this.activePickupY = pickupY;       // ...
        this.activeDropoffX = dropoffX;       // and its dropoff
        this.activeDropoffY = dropoffY;         // ...
        this.currentRiders = 1;                   // now carrying one rider
    }

    public void addPooledRider() { currentRiders++; } // a second rider joins the existing reference route
    public void removeRider() { currentRiders--; }       // a rider's trip completes, freeing a seat
}

// One rider's trip request, tracked through its lifecycle.
class Ride {
    private final String rideId;         // unique id, e.g. RIDE1
    private final String riderName;        // who requested it
    private final double pickupX;             // pickup x coordinate
    private final double pickupY;                // pickup y coordinate
    private final double dropoffX;                  // dropoff x coordinate
    private final double dropoffY;                     // dropoff y coordinate
    private final RideType type;                          // solo or pooled
    private String assignedDriverId;                         // which driver is carrying it, if any
    private RideStatus status;                                 // current lifecycle state

    public Ride(String rideId, String riderName, double pickupX, double pickupY, double dropoffX, double dropoffY, RideType type) {
        this.rideId = rideId;               // store id
        this.riderName = riderName;           // store rider
        this.pickupX = pickupX;                 // store pickup x
        this.pickupY = pickupY;                    // store pickup y
        this.dropoffX = dropoffX;                     // store dropoff x
        this.dropoffY = dropoffY;                        // store dropoff y
        this.type = type;                                  // store type
        this.status = RideStatus.REQUESTED;                    // starts requested, unmatched
    }

    public String getRideId() { return rideId; }                            // id getter
    public String getRiderName() { return riderName; }                         // rider getter
    public double getPickupX() { return pickupX; }                               // pickup x getter
    public double getPickupY() { return pickupY; }                                  // pickup y getter
    public double getDropoffX() { return dropoffX; }                                   // dropoff x getter
    public double getDropoffY() { return dropoffY; }                                      // dropoff y getter
    public RideType getType() { return type; }                                              // type getter
    public String getAssignedDriverId() { return assignedDriverId; }                           // assigned driver getter
    public void setAssignedDriverId(String driverId) { this.assignedDriverId = driverId; }        // assign a driver
    public RideStatus getStatus() { return status; }                                                 // status getter
    public void setStatus(RideStatus status) { this.status = status; }                                  // status setter
}

// Creates sequential, correctly-prefixed ids for rides.
class RideIdFactory {
    private int rideCounter = 0; // running id counter

    public String nextRideId() {
        rideCounter++;                // bump id counter
        return "RIDE" + rideCounter;    // e.g. RIDE1
    }
}

from enum import Enum

# Whether a ride is willing to share a driver with another rider.
class RideType(Enum):
    SOLO = "SOLO"
    POOLED = "POOLED"

# Lifecycle status of a single ride.
class RideStatus(Enum):
    REQUESTED = "REQUESTED"
    MATCHED = "MATCHED"
    COMPLETED = "COMPLETED"

# A courier with a location, a capacity, and the active route of whoever they picked up first.
class Driver:
    def __init__(self, driver_id, location_x, location_y, capacity):
        self.driver_id = driver_id      # unique id
        self.location_x = location_x      # base x coordinate
        self.location_y = location_y        # base y coordinate
        self.capacity = capacity              # max concurrent riders this driver can carry
        self.current_riders = 0                 # starts empty
        self.active_pickup_x = 0.0                 # reference route: first rider's pickup x
        self.active_pickup_y = 0.0                    # reference route: first rider's pickup y
        self.active_dropoff_x = 0.0                      # reference route: first rider's dropoff x
        self.active_dropoff_y = 0.0                         # reference route: first rider's dropoff y

    def is_empty(self):
        return self.current_riders == 0  # true if carrying nobody

    def has_spare_seat(self):
        return self.current_riders < self.capacity  # true if room for one more

    def assign_fresh(self, pickup_x, pickup_y, dropoff_x, dropoff_y):
        self.active_pickup_x = pickup_x      # this becomes the reference route's pickup
        self.active_pickup_y = pickup_y        # ...
        self.active_dropoff_x = dropoff_x        # and its dropoff
        self.active_dropoff_y = dropoff_y          # ...
        self.current_riders = 1                      # now carrying one rider

    def add_pooled_rider(self):
        self.current_riders += 1  # a second rider joins the existing reference route

    def remove_rider(self):
        self.current_riders -= 1  # a rider's trip completes, freeing a seat

# One rider's trip request, tracked through its lifecycle.
class Ride:
    def __init__(self, ride_id, rider_name, pickup_x, pickup_y, dropoff_x, dropoff_y, ride_type):
        self.ride_id = ride_id            # unique id, e.g. RIDE1
        self.rider_name = rider_name        # who requested it
        self.pickup_x = pickup_x              # pickup x coordinate
        self.pickup_y = pickup_y                # pickup y coordinate
        self.dropoff_x = dropoff_x                # dropoff x coordinate
        self.dropoff_y = dropoff_y                  # dropoff y coordinate
        self.type = ride_type                          # solo or pooled
        self.assigned_driver_id = None                    # which driver is carrying it, if any
        self.status = RideStatus.REQUESTED                   # starts requested, unmatched

# Creates sequential, correctly-prefixed ids for rides.
class RideIdFactory:
    def __init__(self):
        self.ride_counter = 0  # running id counter

    def next_ride_id(self):
        self.ride_counter += 1  # bump id counter
        return f"RIDE{self.ride_counter}"  # e.g. RIDE1

import math

# Reusable straight line distance helper.
def distance(x1, y1, x2, y2):
    dx = x2-x1  # x difference
    dy = y2-y1  # y difference
    return math.sqrt(dx * dx + dy * dy)  # Euclidean distance

# Strategy interface: how a driver is chosen for a ride request.
class MatchingStrategy:
    def find_driver(self, ride, drivers): raise NotImplementedError

# Only matches empty drivers, never shares a ride, choosing the nearest one to the pickup.
class DirectMatchingStrategy(MatchingStrategy):
    def find_driver(self, ride, drivers):
        best = None                     # best empty candidate found so far
        best_distance = float("inf")      # distance of the best candidate
        for driver in drivers:              # scan every registered driver
            if not driver.is_empty():
                continue  # solo never shares, skip occupied drivers
            d = distance(driver.location_x, driver.location_y, ride.pickup_x, ride.pickup_y)
            if d < best_distance:  # closer than anything seen so far
                best_distance = d  # remember the new best distance
                best = driver  # remember the new best driver
        return best  # the nearest empty driver, or None if none exist

# Tries a detour constrained insertion into an occupied driver first, falls back to the nearest empty driver.
class PooledMatchingStrategy(MatchingStrategy):
    def __init__(self, max_detour_distance):
        self.max_detour_distance = max_detour_distance  # how much extra distance a pooling insertion may add

    def compute_detour(self, driver, ride):
        original_distance = distance(driver.active_pickup_x, driver.active_pickup_y, driver.active_dropoff_x, driver.active_dropoff_y)
        to_new_pickup = distance(driver.active_pickup_x, driver.active_pickup_y, ride.pickup_x, ride.pickup_y)
        across_new_ride = distance(ride.pickup_x, ride.pickup_y, ride.dropoff_x, ride.dropoff_y)
        to_original_dropoff = distance(ride.dropoff_x, ride.dropoff_y, driver.active_dropoff_x, driver.active_dropoff_y)
        new_distance = to_new_pickup + across_new_ride + to_original_dropoff  # full route with the insertion
        return new_distance-original_distance  # the extra distance this insertion would add

    def find_driver(self, ride, drivers):
        best_pool_candidate = None      # best occupied candidate found so far
        best_detour = float("inf")        # detour of the best candidate
        for driver in drivers:               # scan every registered driver
            if driver.is_empty() or not driver.has_spare_seat():
                continue  # only consider occupied drivers with room
            detour = self.compute_detour(driver, ride)  # extra distance this insertion would add
            if detour <= self.max_detour_distance and detour < best_detour:  # within tolerance and better than seen so far
                best_detour = detour  # remember the new best detour
                best_pool_candidate = driver  # remember the new best pool candidate
        if best_pool_candidate is not None:
            return best_pool_candidate  # a pooling opportunity qualified
        return DirectMatchingStrategy().find_driver(ride, drivers)  # otherwise fall back to the nearest empty driver

# Observer interface: reacts to ride lifecycle events.
class RideObserver:
    def on_ride_matched(self, ride, driver): raise NotImplementedError
    def on_match_failed(self, ride_id, reason): raise NotImplementedError
    def on_ride_completed(self, ride): raise NotImplementedError

# Simple observer that prints events to the console.
class ConsoleRideObserver(RideObserver):
    def on_ride_matched(self, ride, driver):
        print(f"Ride {ride.ride_id} matched to {driver.driver_id}, riders now {driver.current_riders}")

    def on_match_failed(self, ride_id, reason):
        print(f"Match failed for {ride_id}: {reason}")

    def on_ride_completed(self, ride):
        print(f"Ride {ride.ride_id} completed")

# Custom exceptions for the realistic failure modes.
class NoDriverAvailableException(Exception): pass
class InvalidRideStateException(Exception): pass
class DetourLimitExceededException(Exception): pass

# The core ride matching engine tying every piece together.
class RideDispatchService:
    BASE_FARE = 5.0        # flat fare component
    PER_KM_RATE = 2.0        # distance based fare component
    POOL_DISCOUNT = 0.8        # multiplier applied when a ride ends up shared

    def __init__(self, max_detour_distance):
        self.drivers = {}    # driverId -> Driver
        self.rides = {}         # rideId -> Ride
        self.pooled_matching_strategy = PooledMatchingStrategy(max_detour_distance)  # shared instance, so its detour limit is reused
        self.observers = []                                                              # listeners

    def add_driver(self, driver):
        self.drivers[driver.driver_id] = driver  # register a driver

    def add_observer(self, observer):
        self.observers.append(observer)  # register a listener

    def _strategy_for(self, ride_type):
        return DirectMatchingStrategy() if ride_type == RideType.SOLO else self.pooled_matching_strategy  # solo never pools, pooled tries to

    def request_ride(self, rider_name, pickup_x, pickup_y, dropoff_x, dropoff_y, ride_type, factory):
        ride_id = factory.next_ride_id()  # build id
        ride = Ride(ride_id, rider_name, pickup_x, pickup_y, dropoff_x, dropoff_y, ride_type)  # build the ride
        self.rides[ride_id] = ride  # register it
        strategy = self._strategy_for(ride_type)  # pick the matching algorithm for this type
        driver = strategy.find_driver(ride, self.drivers.values())  # ask it for a driver
        if driver is None:  # nobody qualifies
            for obs in self.observers:
                obs.on_match_failed(ride_id, "No driver available")
            raise NoDriverAvailableException(f"No driver available for ride {ride_id}")
        if driver.is_empty():
            driver.assign_fresh(pickup_x, pickup_y, dropoff_x, dropoff_y)  # this driver's first rider defines the reference route
        else:
            driver.add_pooled_rider()  # otherwise this rider joins the existing reference route
        ride.assigned_driver_id = driver.driver_id  # record the assignment
        ride.status = RideStatus.MATCHED  # advance the lifecycle
        for obs in self.observers:
            obs.on_ride_matched(ride, driver)  # notify
        return ride  # hand back the now-matched ride

    def pool_manually(self, ride_id, driver_id, factory):
        ride = self.rides[ride_id]  # the ride to pool
        driver = self.drivers[driver_id]  # the requested driver
        if driver.is_empty() or not driver.has_spare_seat():  # must already be occupied with room, or this is not a pooling case
            raise DetourLimitExceededException(f"Driver {driver_id} is not a valid pooling target")
        detour = self.pooled_matching_strategy.compute_detour(driver, ride)  # extra distance this insertion would add
        if detour > self.pooled_matching_strategy.max_detour_distance:
            raise DetourLimitExceededException(f"Pooling onto {driver_id} would add a detour of {detour}")
        driver.add_pooled_rider()  # this rider joins the existing reference route
        ride.assigned_driver_id = driver_id  # record the assignment
        ride.status = RideStatus.MATCHED  # advance the lifecycle
        for obs in self.observers:
            obs.on_ride_matched(ride, driver)  # notify
        return ride  # hand back the now-matched ride

    def calculate_fare(self, ride_id):
        ride = self.rides[ride_id]  # the ride to price
        driver = self.drivers[ride.assigned_driver_id]  # its assigned driver
        trip_distance = distance(ride.pickup_x, ride.pickup_y, ride.dropoff_x, ride.dropoff_y)  # direct trip distance
        fare = RideDispatchService.BASE_FARE + RideDispatchService.PER_KM_RATE * trip_distance  # base plus distance based component
        if driver.current_riders > 1:
            fare *= RideDispatchService.POOL_DISCOUNT  # apply the pooled discount if actually shared
        return fare  # the computed price

    def complete_ride(self, ride_id):
        ride = self.rides[ride_id]  # the ride to complete
        if ride.status != RideStatus.MATCHED:  # must currently be matched
            raise InvalidRideStateException(f"Ride {ride_id} is not matched, cannot be completed")
        driver = self.drivers[ride.assigned_driver_id]  # its assigned driver
        driver.remove_rider()  # free up their seat
        ride.status = RideStatus.COMPLETED  # advance the lifecycle
        for obs in self.observers:
            obs.on_ride_completed(ride)  # notify
        return ride  # hand back the updated ride

items: Why measure detour as the extra distance a route-insertion adds, rather than simply the distance from the driver to the new rider's pickup? Because a driver could be close to a new pickup yet the insertion could still force a large, unacceptable backtrack before reaching their original destination, the insertion-based detour captures the full cost the existing rider actually experiences.

Why does SOLO refuse to even consider an occupied driver whose detour would technically qualify? Because a rider explicitly choosing not to share is a business rule, not a performance optimization, and DirectMatchingStrategy encodes that rule directly rather than leaving it as an afterthought.

How would you extend this beyond two riders per driver? Represent the driver's route as an ordered list of stops instead of a single pickup and dropoff pair, and generalize the detour calculation to test every valid insertion position for the new stop pair.

Detour-constrained greedy insertion vs a full route-optimization solver: greedy insertion is simple, fast, and easy to reason about, at the cost of not finding the globally optimal pooling arrangement across every driver and rider at once; a full solver could do better but is far more complex and slower to compute at scale.

Capping pooling at two riders vs a full multi-stop route: a two-rider cap keeps the detour math tractable and easy to verify, at the cost of missing pooling opportunities across three or more riders that a full route representation could capture.

Fare computed at completion vs fare locked in at match time: computing at completion correctly rewards early poolers if someone joins them later, at the cost of a rider not knowing their exact final fare the moment they are matched.
Persist drivers and rides in a database using the schema in the Database Design section, with driver location and occupancy also cached in a fast key-value store for low-latency matching.
Emit match and completion events to a message queue so downstream systems (rider notifications, driver apps, analytics) can consume them asynchronously instead of via in-process observers.
Shard driver tracking by geographic region in a large-scale deployment, so a ride request only scans nearby drivers instead of every driver system-wide.
Track driver location via periodic GPS updates rather than a static coordinate, and re-run detour calculations against the freshest available location.
